title: P and D
summary: Two new keys: P and D. The finger goes out, presses, and comes back.
intro: Two new keys in this lesson: P and D. They belong to your right ring finger and your left ring finger. The movement is always the same — out, press, back — and the way back is the part being trained, because a finger left out of place spoils the next letter.
congrats: Two more keys under your fingers. If P and D already come without searching, the lesson has done its job.

screens.text: This key belongs to your right ring finger. Find it without looking, press it once, and let the finger return. The way back matters as much as the press.
Only P and what you already know. Slowly, and bring the finger back to the home row after every press.
screens.content:
p p pp
pppp
pppppp pppppp

screens.text: This key belongs to your left ring finger. Find it without looking, press it once, and let the finger return. The way back matters as much as the press.
Only D and what you already know. Slowly, and bring the finger back to the home row after every press.
screens.content:
pdpd dpdp
pd dp
dht pn dh

screens.text: Short groups, one after another. Keep going to the end even if you miss one.
The new keys mixed with the old ones, which is how they will turn up inside words.
screens.content:
thp ens th
np pn npnp
ppp ddd ttt nnnn

screens.text: Real words with the new keys. Type each word in one go, not letter by letter.
screens.content:
dish drags ready need
under bridge ahead regards
door read page reads

screens.text: A burst of short words with the new keys in them.
Now the weight is on P, the one you have pressed least.
screens.content:
body ship sheep trees
wash others suit dish
south sages white speed

screens.text: Back to patterns for a moment, to check that the fingers still find their way home.
screens.content:
pdpdpd dpdpdp
pd dp
dph tn dp

screens.text: Everything you have, mixed together. Notice how many words already come without thinking.
